title: Jerusalem's Epic Fail

EN 6번 문단(배지 '7'): MSG '비웃고, 또 비웃었다' 반복 복원

EN 20번 문단(배지 '21'): MSG 'Bring on Judgment Day!' 명칭 복원
paragraphs: Man, look at this city. It used to be so crowded, but now it's a ghost town. She's a widow now — she used to be the queen of all nations, and now she's basically a slave.
She's up all night crying, tears just pouring down her face. And out of all her so-called friends, not a single one is there for her. They all betrayed her and became her enemies.

Judah got dragged away into exile, totally defeated and forced into hard labor. Now she's living among foreigners with no place to even chill. Her enemies caught up to her and trapped her in a tight spot.
Zion's roads are weeping, empty of pilgrims headed to the feasts. The city gates are deserted, the priests are all sighing, and the young women are grieving. It's a super bitter situation.
Her enemies are in charge now, living their best life while she's suffering. And it's because God brought this on her for all her screw-ups. Her own kids were captured and taken away by the enemy.
All the beauty has drained from Daughter Zion's face. Her leaders are like starving deer that can't find any grass. They're weak and running with no energy left, with the enemy hot on their trail.

Jerusalem can't stop thinking about the good old days, and how she lost it all. Her people were captured by the enemy, and there was no one to help. Her enemies just stared and laughed — laughed at her helpless silence.

Jerusalem seriously messed up, and now she's a total outcast. Everyone who used to look up to her now looks down on her because they've seen her dark side. She's just groaning and hiding her face in shame.

She was living wild and didn't care about the future, and now she's had a legendary crash. There's no one to give her a hand. She's crying out, "God, look at my pain! See how the enemy is flexing on me."
The enemy came in and snatched all her precious things. She had to watch as pagans, the very people you told to stay out, barged right into her holy Sanctuary.
All the people are groaning, desperate for a crumb of bread. They're trading their favorite things just to get a little food to stay alive. "God, look at me! Worthless, cheap, abject!"
"Yo, all you people walking by, pay attention! Have you ever seen pain like my pain? Have you seen what God did to me when he was furious?"
"He sent down fire from the sky that went straight through my bones. He set a trap for my feet and knocked me down. He left me totally wrecked and sick all day long."
"My sins were all bundled up and tied like a yoke on my neck. He made me so weak that I couldn't fight back when my enemies took over. The Lord handed me over to them."
"The Lord rejected all my best warriors. He sent an army to crush my young men. He stomped on the virgin daughter of Judah like she was a grape in a winepress."
"This is why I'm bawling my eyes out. Tears are streaming down my face. There's no one here to comfort me or give me strength. My children are ruined because the enemy was just too strong."
Zion is reaching out her hands, but there's no one to help her. God ordered enemies to surround Jacob's people. Now Jerusalem is like a filthy rag that everyone avoids.
"God is totally in the right; I'm the one who rebelled against his word. Listen up, everyone! Look at my suffering. My young men and women have all been dragged into exile."
"I called out to my friends, but they completely ghosted me. My priests and leaders were starving in the city, trying to find food just to stay alive, but they couldn't even save themselves."
"God, look at the mess I'm in! My stomach is in knots, and my heart is twisted because I've been such a rebel. Outside, there's violence in the streets, and inside, it feels like death."

"People hear me groaning, but no one comforts me. All my enemies heard about the disaster you sent, and they're actually happy about it. Bring on Judgment Day — the day you promised! Let them get what I got!"
"Look at how evil they are. Do to them what you did to me because of all my sins. I'm groaning nonstop, and my heart is completely broken."

title: God's Fury? Total Meltdown in Zion

paragraphs: Man... God seriously just wrecked Daughter Zion. It's like he took Israel, his prized possession, and just chucked it in the trash. Straight up dropped it from the sky.
God didn't even hesitate. He just swallowed Israel whole, crushing all of Judah's defenses in his fury, totally wrecking their king and leaders.
He was so mad, he just flattened Israel. Snapped their strength in half and then bounced right when the enemy showed up. Then he came at Jacob like a wildfire from all sides.
He acted like a straight-up enemy. Lined up his shot, pulled out his sword, and took out all our best and brightest young guys. His rage was like a fire that torched every house in Zion.
God became the enemy. He devoured Israel, chewing up all their defenses. Now Daughter Judah is left moaning and groaning.
He wrecked his own Temple, his special meeting place. God erased all memory of feast days and Sabbaths in Zion. He was so mad he got rid of the king and the priests too.
God just bailed on his own altar and temple. Handed the keys over to the enemy. And they were in there celebrating like it was some big party.
God literally made a blueprint to tear down Daughter Zion's walls. Got his crew together and they went to town. It was a total demolition job. Even the rocks were crying.

The city gates, the iron bars, everything just vanished into dust. The kings and leaders got shipped off to who-knows-where, so there was no one left to guide us. And the prophets? They were useless. They weren't getting any messages from God.

The old leaders of Daughter Zion are just sitting on the ground, not saying a word. They're throwing dirt on their heads and wearing scratchy clothes to show how sorry they are. The young women of Jerusalem have their faces all streaked with grime.
I've cried so much I can't see straight. My stomach is in knots; my insides have turned to jelly over what's happened to my people. Little kids are passing out everywhere.
They're crying out to their moms, 'I'm hungry! I'm thirsty!' and then just collapsing in the streets like wounded soldiers, taking their last breath in their mothers' arms.

How am I supposed to get what you're going through, Jerusalem? What can I even say to make you feel better, Zion? Who can fix this for you? This whole situation is just a disaster, it's beyond messed up.

Your prophets were just telling you what you wanted to hear. They didn't call you out on your mistakes so you could actually change. Their sermons were just a bunch of wishful thinking and false visions.
People walking by are shook. They can't believe their eyes. They're just staring at Jerusalem like, 'Is this for real? Is this the city they voted "Most Beautiful" and "Best Place to Live"?'
But now your enemies are just staring with their mouths open. Then they start rubbing their hands together all happy, like, 'We got 'em! We've been waiting for this! Here it is!'

God really did everything he said he would, step by step. He always warned this would happen. And now he's done it—he's torn the whole place down. He let your enemies walk all over you and basically crowned them the new champs.
Just cry your heart out to God, dear repentant Zion. Let your tears flow like a river, day and night. Don't stop, no breaks. Just keep crying.

Every night, when the watch starts, get up and just pour out your heart in prayer. Talk to God like you're face to face. Lift up your hands and beg him to save your kids who are starving to death in the streets.

'God, just look at us. Seriously, think about it. Have you ever done this to anyone else? Should moms be eating their own babies, the kids they raised? Should priests and prophets be murdered in the Master's own Sanctuary?'
'Young guys and old men are just lying dead in the streets. My best young men and women were killed. You were so angry you killed them without any mercy, just cut them down in cold blood.'
'You invited these attackers to come down on us like they were your friends coming to a party. So on the day of your great anger, nobody escaped. The kids I loved and raised — gone, gone, gone.'

title: From Rock Bottom to Real Hope
changes: 3장: MSG 전 22유닛(절구간 1-3~64-66) 대조 — Teen 22문단 1:1 대응 확인

paragraphs: I'm the guy who's seen some serious trouble, the kind that comes straight from God's anger. He grabbed my hand and walked me straight into pitch-black darkness. And yeah, He's been hitting me with setback after setback, non-stop.

He basically wasted me away to nothing but skin and bones, and then broke them. He cornered me, ganged up on me, and just dumped all this trouble and hardship on me. He locked me away in the deepest darkness, like a corpse nailed shut inside a coffin.

He's boxed me in so I can't escape, like I'm in handcuffs and leg chains. Even when I scream and beg for help, it's like He just ignores my prayers, like He's locked them up and tossed the key. He's built walls around me with massive stones. I'm totally trapped.

He's like a bear stalking me, a lion hiding and ready to jump. He threw me off my path and tore me to shreds. When He was done, there was nothing left of me. He then used me for target practice with his bow and arrows.
He shot me right in the gut with his arrows. Everyone treats me like a joke, the main character in their diss tracks. He made me eat disgusting, rotten food and drink nasty stuff until I was bloated.

He smashed my face into the gravel and ground me into the dirt. I completely gave up on life. I can't even remember what being happy feels like. I told myself, "This is it. I'm done. Believing in God is pointless now."

I'll never forget the struggle, feeling so lost, the taste of ashes, the poison I had to swallow. I remember it all—man, I remember it so clearly—that feeling of hitting rock bottom. But there's this one other thing I remember, and holding onto that memory gives me hope:

God's love is loyal and it never runs out; His mercy never dries up. They are brand new every single morning. Your faithfulness is insane! I'm sticking with God (I keep saying it over and over). He's all I have left.

God is good to the person who waits for Him with everything they've got, to the one who seriously seeks Him out. It's a good thing to quietly hope, to quietly wait for help from God. It's also good to push through the hard times when you're young.

When life gets super heavy and hard to handle, just go be by yourself. Get into the quiet. Bow down and pray. Don't ask a bunch of questions: just wait for hope to show up. Don't run from your problems. Face them head-on. The "worst" thing that can happen is never actually the worst.

Why? Because the Lord will never just leave and not come back. If He's harsh, He's also gentle. His supply of loyal love is massive. He doesn't get any joy out of making life hard or putting obstacles in our way:
Stomping on helpless prisoners, denying justice to victims in the court of the Most High God, messing with the evidence—the Lord is not okay with any of that.

Who do you think just says something and it happens? It's the Lord who gives those orders. Doesn't the Most High God create everything, the good stuff and the hard stuff? And why would anyone who's been given life complain when they're punished for their own mistakes?

Let's take a hard look at how we're living and get our lives right with God. Let's lift up our hearts and our hands at the same time, praying to God in heaven: "We've been stubborn and rebellious, and you haven't forgiven us.

"You got angry with us and didn't hold back. You chased us down and killed us without any mercy. You wrapped yourself in a thick cloud so none of our prayers could get through. You treated us like dirty dishwater and threw us out in the backyard of the nations.

"Our enemies are yelling insults at us, their mouths full of hate, just spitting venom. We've been through hell and back. We have nowhere to turn, nowhere to go. Rivers of tears are pouring from my eyes because my people are so broken.

"The tears just keep streaming from my eyes, like a non-stop fountain, until you, God, look down from heaven and see my pain. When I see what's happened to the young women in my city, my heart just breaks.

"Enemies who had no reason to hate me hunted me down like a bird. They threw me into a pit and then threw stones at me. Then the rains came and filled the pit. The water went over my head. I thought, 'It's all over.'

"I called out your name, O God, from the very bottom of that pit. You heard me when I cried out, 'Don't close your ears to me! Get me out of here! Save me!' You came close when I called. You said, 'It's going to be okay.'
"You took my side, Lord; you saved my life! God, you saw all the wrong they did to me. Now, give me justice! Yeah, you saw their evil plans, all their plots to destroy me.

"You heard them, God, their nasty gossip, their secret plots to ruin me. They never stop, these enemies of mine, just thinking up trouble, planning evil, day after day after day. Whether they're sitting or standing—just look at them!—they make fun of me with their vulgar songs.
"Make them pay for what they've done, God. Give them what they deserve. Break their miserable hearts! Curse them! Get really angry. Hunt them down. Completely destroy them from under your heavens!"

paragraphs: Oh man, for real... How is gold now treated like dirt, the best gold just tossed out with the trash? Priceless jewels are scattered everywhere, just lying in the gutters.
The people of Zion, who used to be so highly valued, worth way more than gold, are now treated like cheap clay pots, the kind you can get anywhere.
Even wild animals like jackals feed their babies, you know? But my own people have become cruel to their kids, like ostriches that just abandon their eggs in the desert.
Babies are so thirsty their tongues are stuck to the roofs of their mouths. Little kids are begging for food, but nobody gives them even a single crumb.
People who used to eat at the best tables are now scrounging for scraps in the streets. The ones who wore fine clothes are digging through trash piles for something to wear.
The messed-up things my people did were even worse than what Sodom did. That city was destroyed in an instant, with no one to even help them.

The leaders, who were once so healthy and glowing — their beards like carved stone — are now covered in soot. You wouldn't even recognize them on the street. They're just skin and bones, their skin all dry and leathery.
Honestly, it would've been better to die in a battle than to die of starvation. At least getting killed by a sword is quick, instead of slowly wasting away.
This is wild, but kind women actually boiled their own children for food. That was the only thing to eat when my people were completely broken.
God just let all His anger out, no holding back. He poured out all His fury and set a fire in Zion that burned the whole place to the ground.
Kings and rulers all over the world were shook. They couldn't believe it when they saw enemies just marching right into Jerusalem's gates like they owned the place.
This all happened because of the sins of the prophets and the evil of the priests. They totally took advantage of good people and basically ruined their lives.

Now those same prophets and priests are blindly stumbling around the streets, grimy and stained, dressed in rags from their wasted lives. People yell at them, 'Get out of here! Get lost! Don't touch us — don't infect us!' They have to leave town; nobody wants them around. Everyone knows they got kicked out of their own hometown.
God Himself scattered them. He's not looking out for them anymore. He's done with the priests and doesn't care about the elders.
We kept watching and watching, wore our eyes out looking for help, but got nothing. We posted our lookouts and waited for rescue that never showed up.
They hunted us down. It wasn't even safe to walk in the streets. We knew our end was coming; our days were numbered. We were totally doomed.
They were faster than eagles, chasing us in the mountains and setting traps for us in the desert.
Our king, the one God chose, who was like our life-source, got caught in their traps. We always thought we'd be safe under his protection, but nope.
So go ahead and celebrate, Edom — live it up in Uz! Because your turn is coming. You're going to drink from the same cup of God's wrath, get drunk on it, and wake up stripped naked with nothing.
And that's a wrap for you, Zion. Your punishment is over. You won't have to go through this exile again. But Edom, your judgment is coming. God's gonna expose all your sin for everyone to see.

title: God, Are You Ghosting Us?!

paragraphs: God, seriously, look at what we've been through. Our reputation is totally wrecked. Our awesome land has been handed over to a bunch of strangers, and our homes to people we don't even know. We're basically orphans, with no dads around, and our moms are pretty much widows.

We literally have to pay for our own water. Even the wood for our fires has a price tag. We're getting pushed around and bossed like slaves, totally worn out with zero breaks. We literally sold ourselves out to Assyria and Egypt just to get food on the table.
Our parents messed up and they're not here anymore, but now we're paying for all the wrong things they did. We're being ruled by slaves, and there's no way to escape their grip.
We have to risk our lives just to find food in the desert, which is crawling with bandits. The hunger has been so bad that our skin is as black as an oven and feels like old, dried-out leather.

Our wives were raped right in the streets of Zion, and our young girls in the towns of Judah. They hung our leaders by their hands and showed no respect to our elders. Strong young guys were forced to do women's work, and even little boys had to do men's heavy labor.

The wise elders don't hang out at the city gate anymore. The sound of young people making music is gone. All the joy has been sucked out of our lives. Our dance parties have turned into funeral marches.

The crown of glory has fallen right off our heads. Woe! Woe! Man, we really messed up by sinning. Because of all this, we're completely heartbroken; we can't even see straight through our tears. Mount Zion is a total ruin, just a hangout spot for jackals.

But look, God, you're still the King, right? Your throne is eternal. So why does it feel like you've forgotten us? Why would you just dump us and leave us hanging like this? Please, bring us back to you, God—we're so ready to come back. Give us a fresh start. Because right now, it feels like you've totally disowned us. You've been seriously angry with us.
